Apex Industrial Dynamics Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Dynamics Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Dynamics Corp.'s performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering robust demand signals across our core industrial equipment portfolio. We've seen a strong book-to-bill ratio trending higher, reflecting excellent visibility into future revenue from our record backlog. Order intake accelerated across key end markets like construction, mining, and agriculture, with healthy year-over-year growth underscoring our market position. Revenue grew solidly in all geographic regions, particularly North America, while favorable price-cost dynamics bolstered our margins despite input pressures. Supply chain constraints have eased notably, enabling better on-time delivery, and we're providing raised operating margin guidance for the quarter ahead and full year. These results position us exceptionally well for sustained growth in factory automation, precision machining, and material handling.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Thompson to provide more detail on our financial results.

David Thompson (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Dynamics Corp. reported $1.35 billion in revenue for the third quarter, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.2%, driven by favorable product mix, pricing discipline, and supply chain efficiencies. Operating expenses were $215 million, resulting in an operating income of $180 million. Our net income for the quarter was $135 million, or $1.42 per share.

I'll now turn to our book-to-bill dynamics, which continue to underscore the strength in our order pipeline and provide excellent visibility into future revenue streams. As you know, in the industrial equipment sector, the book-to-bill ratio—calculated as total orders booked divided by total revenue recognized in the period—is a critical leading indicator of demand momentum, backlog growth, and our ability to sustain mid-teens organic growth amid ongoing supply chain normalization and customer capex recovery.

For the third quarter, we delivered a company-wide book-to-bill ratio of 1.18x, marking a sequential improvement from 1.12x in Q2 and a year-over-year increase from 1.05x in Q3 2023. This is our strongest quarterly reading since Q4 2021, pre-supply disruptions, and reflects robust demand across our core segments: Factory Automation Systems, Precision Machining Centers, and Material Handling Equipment. For context, our trailing 12-month book-to-bill now stands at 1.14x, which has driven backlog expansion to a record $4.2 billion, up 22% year-over-year and representing approximately 2.1x our quarterly revenue run-rate. This backlog provides high-confidence visibility into 85% of our projected 2025 revenue, with 65% weighted toward high-margin, software-enabled systems.

Diving into segment trends, our Factory Automation business—powered by our next-gen collaborative robots and IoT-integrated PLCs—led the way with a stellar 1.25x book-to-bill. Orders here surged 28% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by hyperscaler data center builds and automotive OEMs ramping EV battery assembly lines. We're seeing particular strength in our Fanuc-compatible cobot platforms, where customers like Tesla and Foxconn are deploying our systems for high-mix, low-volume production to counter labor shortages. Margins in this segment held at 32%, benefiting from our strategic shift toward as-a-service models, where 40% of new bookings now include multi-year software subscriptions for predictive maintenance via our DynamicsEdge platform.

Precision Machining Centers came in at 1.15x, up from 1.08x last quarter, as aerospace and defense exposure offset softer semi-capex. Bookings from Boeing and Lockheed Martin suppliers jumped 35%, driven by our 5-axis CNC mills with adaptive control tech that reduce cycle times by 25% on titanium alloys—critical for next-gen aircraft like the 777X. However, we did see some lumpiness in semiconductor fab equipment orders, down 10% sequentially due to inventory digestion at TSMC and Samsung fabs, though our backlog here remains healthy at $1.1 billion.

Material Handling rounded out at 1.10x, steady but with upside potential as e-commerce logistics rebounds. Orders for our automated guided vehicles and sortation systems grew 15%, with wins at Amazon fulfillment centers and DHL hubs in Europe. Pricing discipline held firm, with a 4.2% realized price increase, supported by steel and component cost stabilization post the 2022-23 inflation spike.

Regionally, North America was the standout at 1.22x, propelled by reshoring tailwinds under the CHIPS Act and Inflation Reduction Act. U.S. bookings rose 30% year-over-year, with hyperscalers like Microsoft expanding AI server fabs and onshoring critical minerals processing—our electromechanical ore crushers saw particular uptake from Freeport-McMoRan. EMEA delivered 1.16x, bolstered by German Mittelstand manufacturers investing in Industry 4.0 upgrades ahead of EU carbon border taxes; we've secured follow-on orders for our Siemens-compatible HMI systems from Bosch and ThyssenKrupp. Asia-Pacific lagged slightly at 1.08x, pressured by China's property sector weakness and delayed capex at Foxconn iPhone lines, though India offset this with 45% growth in orders for textile automation from Reliance Industries.

Strategically, these trends validate our $500 million capex plan for FY25, including a new 400,000 sq ft facility in Spartanburg, SC, to add 20% capacity for cobot and AGV assembly by H2 2025. We're also accelerating R&D in sustainable tech—our eco-friendly, waterless coolant systems for machining centers have won ESG-linked contracts worth $250 million, aligning with customer mandates from the likes of John Deere and Caterpillar. Looking ahead, we expect book-to-bill to hold in the 1.15x-1.20x range through year-end, assuming no major geopolitical disruptions in the Red Sea or Taiwan Strait, which could impact component lead times.

This positions us exceptionally well against peers—our ratio outperforms Honeywell's recent 1.10x and Kuka Robotics' 1.07x—giving us pricing power and share gains in a market projected by Gardner Intelligence to grow 5.8% in machine tool orders for 2025.

Good morning, everyone. As we dive into the details, I'd like to focus on our order intake and book-to-bill dynamics by end market, which remain a strong leading indicator of our future revenue trajectory. Overall, Q3 order intake came in at $2.85 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% sequentially from Q2. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth in orders, driven by robust demand across our core end markets and our continued execution on capacity expansions.

Our company-wide book-to-bill ratio stood at 1.28x for the quarter—comfortably above 1.0x—which has grown our backlog to a record $12.4 billion, up 18% YoY. This provides excellent visibility into 2024 and beyond, with approximately 65% of backlog expected to convert within the next 12 months. Let me break this down by key end markets, where we've seen differentiated performance tied to macro tailwinds, our product innovation pipeline, and targeted share gains against peers like Caterpillar, Komatsu, and CNH Industrial.

Construction end market, representing 42% of Q3 orders, totaled $1.20 billion, surging 22% YoY. Book-to-bill here expanded to 1.45x, fueled by pent-up demand from infrastructure megaprojects. In North America, which accounted for 55% of segment orders, we're seeing outsized wins tied to the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act—think data center builds and highway expansions—where our Cat 793F-class haulers and Liebherr-style large excavators are in high demand. We booked several multi-unit deals exceeding $100 million each for electric mini-excavators, leveraging our new Lynx EV platform, which offers 20% lower TCO through battery swapping and telematics integration. Regionally, EMEA grew 15% YoY amid EU NextGenerationEU funding, but APAC softened 5% due to China's property sector headwinds—though we're mitigating this with localization efforts at our new Wuxi facility, ramping hybrid wheel loaders. Strategically, we're gaining 200 basis points of market share in the 20-50 ton excavator segment via our FastFill autonomous fueling tech, which reduces downtime by 30%. Looking forward, we expect construction orders to moderate to mid-teens growth in Q4 as lead times normalize from 6-9 months.

Mining end market, 28% of Q3 orders, reached $800 million, up 9% YoY, with a book-to-bill of 1.35x. Commodity prices remain supportive—copper up 15% YTD, iron ore stable above $100/tonne—driving capex from majors like Rio Tinto and BHP. Our ultra-class haul trucks, akin to the Komatsu 980E, secured $250 million in orders, including a landmark 15-unit fleet for a greenfield lithium mine in Australia, where our Battery Electric Vehicle rigid dump trucks are deploying with Troy Mine-grade autonomy software for Level 4 operations. North America and APAC each contributed 40% of mining orders, with LATAM up 25% on Peruvian copper ramps. Challenges persist in South Africa due to load-shedding, but our edge in predictive maintenance via IoT-enabled systems has won us stickiness—uptime averaging 95% vs. industry 88%. We're investing $150 million in R&D for hydrogen fuel cell loaders, targeting TRL 7 by mid-2024, positioning us ahead of Sandvik's electric pivot. Backlog here implies 20% revenue growth in FY24.

Agriculture end market, 18% of Q3 orders, hit $510 million, flat YoY but up 8% sequentially, with book-to-bill at 1.10x amid weather volatility. Strong US corn/soy yields boosted demand for high-horsepower tractors—our TerraForce 600 booked $120 million including precision ag suites with RTK GPS and AI yield mapping. Brazil, 35% of segment orders, saw robust sugarcane harvester intake despite El Niño risks, while Europe dipped 10% on subsidy delays. We're countering margin pressures from input costs with our FarmConnect digital platform, integrating analytics for 15% fuel savings. Share gains of 150 bps in row-crop tractors come from modular electrification kits, with first hybrid sprayers shipping Q1. Expect low-single-digit growth into 2024, accelerating with La Niña recovery.

Other end markets, 12% of Q3 orders, saw oil & gas grow 14% YoY on LNG expansions, power gen up 10% with gas turbine ancillaries, and marine steady. Book-to-bill averaged 1.20x.

In summary, our diversified portfolio and tech leadership—electrification now 25% of orders, up from 10% last year—de-risk us amid cycles. We're on track for $11.5-12 billion in FY23 revenue, with Q4 orders guiding to $2.9-3.1 billion.

Good afternoon, everyone. As a leader in precision CNC machining centers, robotic automation systems, and smart factory solutions for the manufacturing sector, we're pleased to report another quarter of robust top-line growth. Let me dive into our revenue performance by geographic region, which highlights the diversification of our $5.2 billion trailing twelve-month book of business. We continue to benefit from a balanced portfolio, with no single region exceeding 48% of total revenue, reducing exposure to regional cyclicality.

North America, 47% of revenue at $602 million, up 18% YoY and 7% QoQ, remains our largest and highest-growth region, fueled by U.S. reshoring initiatives and the CHIPS and Science Act's $52 billion in semiconductor incentives. Revenue here was propelled by a 25% surge in orders for our next-gen RoboForge robotic welding cells, which integrate AI-driven adaptive controls for EV battery production lines—think partnerships with the likes of Tesla and GM's Factory ZERO. Aerospace OEMs, including Boeing and Spirit AeroSystems, contributed another 15% uplift via our high-precision 5-axis CNC mills compliant with ITAR regulations. Margins expanded 220 basis points to 28% on the back of localized supply chains, with 60% of North American content now sourced from U.S. and Mexican facilities under our nearshoring strategy. Sequentially, growth accelerated due to easier comps from last year's port strikes, but we see sustained momentum with our new $150 million expansion of the Rockford, Illinois plant, adding 20% capacity for modular automation skids by Q4.

Europe, 24% of revenue at $307 million, up 8% YoY and flat QoQ, was solid but tempered by persistent energy headwinds and slower industrial capex amid the ECB's hawkish stance. Germany and Italy drove 65% of the region's topline, with strength in our EuroForge series of energy-efficient hydraulic presses for wind turbine components, aligning with the EU Green Deal's 55% emissions reduction target by 2030. Notable wins include a €120 million multi-year contract with Siemens Energy for gearbox machining systems and follow-on orders from Vestas for blade tooling. However, softness in automotive—down 5% due to VW Group's ID.4 production delays—offset some gains, keeping overall growth modest. FX translation from a weaker euro shaved 2 points off reported growth, but on a constant-currency basis, it was +10%. Looking ahead, our strategic pivot to sustainable tech, like CO2-neutral coolant systems, positions us well for REPowerEU funding, and we're targeting mid-teens growth in H2 as German Ifo PMI stabilizes above 90.

Asia-Pacific, 25% of revenue at $320 million, up 16% YoY and 6% QoQ, delivered standout results, underscoring our deep market penetration in high-growth semiconductors and electronics assembly. China accounted for 55% of the segment, with explosive demand for our PrecisionLink IoT-connected pallet systems in Foxconn's iPhone lines and SMIC's 5nm fab expansions—revenue from chip-related equipment jumped 30% YoY. India emerged as a bright spot, contributing $45 million (+40% YoY) via our Tata Motors deal for stamping presses in their Harrier SUV EV transition. Japan and Southeast Asia added tailwinds from Fanuc-compatible robotic end-effectors for collaborative robots in aging workforces. Challenges included U.S. export controls on advanced lithography tools, which we navigated via licensed JVs, but tariffs remain a 1-2% margin drag. Our $100 million investment in a Singapore R&D hub for edge-computing upgrades to our Nexus OS software platform is yielding early wins, with 15% of APAC installs now featuring predictive maintenance analytics that boost OEE by 12% on average.

Rest of World, 4% of revenue at $51 million, up 12% YoY and 3% QoQ, grew steadily on selective exposure. Brazil's Petrobras ramp-up in offshore rig retrofits drove $20 million in subsea valve machining orders, while Saudi Aramco's Vision 2030 giga-projects fueled demand for our heat-resistant alloys in gas compression equipment. Margins here are premium at 32%, reflecting bespoke engineering content.

Geographically, we're accelerating derisking: North America share up 300 bps YoY to 47%, while APAC's resilience offsets Europe's volatility. Key initiatives include our 'ForgeForward' platform—cloud-integrated digital twins reducing setup times by 40%—rolled out across 70% of new installs, enhancing stickiness with 95% renewal rates on service contracts. We're also doubling down on sustainability, with 40% of Q2 revenue from low-carbon certified products, tapping into ESG mandates like the SEC's climate disclosures. Backlog stands at a record $4.1 billion (+22% YoY), with 60% weighted to H2 delivery. For FY2024, we guide regional growth of 12-15% overall, assuming no major trade escalations.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into the impact of price-cost dynamics on our margins, which was a key driver of our outperformance this quarter. In the manufacturing and industrial equipment sector, where we design and produce high-precision CNC machining centers, automated material handling systems like AGVs and AS/RS, and heavy-duty hydraulic presses, margins are highly sensitive to volatile input costs—primarily steel, aluminum, copper, and increasingly semiconductors for our smart factory solutions. We've navigated a challenging macro environment marked by lingering supply chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions from the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and elevated energy prices, yet delivered gross margin expansion of 230 basis points year-over-year to 28.5%, with adjusted EBITDA margins hitting 14.2%, up from 12.1% in Q2 last year.

Raw material costs, which represent about 55% of our COGS, rose 12% sequentially and 18% year-over-year in Q2. Steel prices, our largest input at roughly 35% of material costs, surged 22% YoY, driven by constrained supply from blast furnace outages in Europe and tariff-related distortions in global trade flows—similar to what Caterpillar and Nucor have reported in their recent updates. Aluminum was up 15%, fueled by bauxite shortages and hydropower constraints in China, while copper climbed 25% amid U.S.-China trade frictions and EV-related demand pull from downstream sectors. Semiconductor costs for our IoT-enabled equipment, like our ApexForge CNC series, increased 10% due to ongoing fab capacity tightness at TSMC and Samsung. Freight and logistics added another 8% to our landed costs, with ocean rates from Asia-Pacific up 30% on Red Sea disruptions.

That said, our proactive pricing actions more than offset these pressures, delivering a favorable price-cost mix that expanded gross margins for the fifth straight quarter. We implemented targeted price increases averaging 6.5% across our portfolio, with higher hikes of 8-10% on premium segments like our robotic welding systems and energy-efficient hydraulic presses, where customers prioritize uptime and ESG compliance over sticker price. Average selling prices rose 7.2% YoY, outpacing input inflation by 450 basis points. This pass-through was most effective in North America, where capex strength in reshoring projects—think Intel's Ohio fabs and Tesla's Texas Gigafactory expansions—gave us pricing power; we captured 9% ASP growth there versus flat pricing in EMEA. Importantly, we avoided broad-based hikes that could erode market share, instead using value-based selling tied to our ApexEdge digital twin software, which boosts customer OEE by 15-20% and justifies premiums.

Regionally, the dynamics played out differently. In North America, which drove 52% of Q2 revenue, price-cost favorability added 310 basis points to gross margins, pushing them to 30.8%—well above peers like Deere & Company. Europe, at 28% of sales, faced headwinds from the energy crisis, with natural gas surcharges inflating steel costs an extra 5%; here, margins held steady at 25.2% thanks to 7% pricing and our hedging program covering 45% of euro-denominated steel exposure. Asia-Pacific, 20% of mix, saw softer pricing at 4% growth amid weak Chinese demand for material handling equipment, but our localization strategy in India and Vietnam mitigated forex risks, limiting margin contraction to 50 basis points.

We've ramped our commodity hedging to 50% of forecasted 2024 exposure—up from 30% last year—locking in steel at $750/ton versus spot at $920. Supply chain diversification, including dual-sourcing from U.S. minimills like Steel Dynamics and Brazilian producers, reduced Asia dependency from 40% to 25%. Value engineering on our next-gen AGV fleet shaved 3% off BOM costs through lightweight aluminum alloys and generative design AI, while our supplier collaboration portal enforced cost-down targets averaging 5% annually. Aftermarket services, now 22% of revenue with 45% gross margins, provided a natural hedge—recurring parts and predictive maintenance from our ApexPredict platform grew 15% YoY, insulating us from OEM pricing volatility.

Strategically, we're positioning for sustained margin expansion to 30%+ gross by year-end. We'll lean into premiumization, targeting 60% mix in high-margin smart equipment akin to Ingersoll Rand's integrated solutions. Selective M&A, like our tuck-in of a German hydraulic actuator specialist, bolsters vertical integration. And with U.S. IRA incentives driving industrial capex, we're guiding for 8-10% ASP realization in H2, assuming steel stabilizes around $850/ton.

In summary, disciplined price-cost management turned a 18% input headwind into 230 basis points of tailwind, underscoring our resilience in this cyclical industry.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before I dive into the segment details, I'd like to highlight our total order intake, which continues to serve as a strong leading indicator of our revenue trajectory and underscores the resilience of our end-markets in the industrial equipment space.

For Q3, we recorded total order intake of $1.28 billion, representing a robust 18% year-over-year growth on an organic basis, excluding the impact of FX which headwinded us by about 2 points due to the strengthening USD. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY order growth, bringing our trailing twelve-month order intake to a record $5.1 billion, up 22% from the prior year. Our book-to-bill ratio expanded to 1.22x for the quarter—up from 1.15x a year ago and 1.18x in Q2—reflecting healthy demand outpacing our shipment capacity as we methodically ramp utilization across our global footprint.

By business unit, Discrete Automation Solutions, 38% of total orders, surged 28% YoY to $488 million. This segment, including our FANUC-compatible robotic arms, collaborative robots, and vision-guided assembly systems, benefited from accelerated factory automation investments. Customers in automotive and semiconductor sectors are prioritizing our NexGen AI platform, which integrates machine learning for predictive path optimization and reduces cycle times by up to 25%. We saw particular strength in palletizing and depalletizing systems, with several multi-year framework agreements signed for high-volume deployments.

Process Equipment & Heavy Machinery, 32% of orders, grew 12% YoY to $410 million, driven by our turbomachinery lineup, including centrifugal compressors and steam turbines. The push toward electrification and decarbonization is a tailwind here; we secured $150 million in orders for hydrogen-ready compressors tied to blue hydrogen initiatives in the Middle East and Europe. Pricing discipline added 4 points to this growth, as input cost inflation has stabilized.

Material Handling & Storage Systems, 20% of orders, hit $256 million, up 22% YoY, fueled by e-commerce and logistics reshoring. Our AS/RS saw uptake from clients like Amazon Robotics partners and Prologis warehouse developers. The integration of our IoT-enabled digital twin software enables 15-20% throughput improvements and remote diagnostics.

Aerospace & Defense Aftermarket, 10% of orders, was steady at $128 million, up 8% YoY, with strength in MRO services for turbine components. Geopolitical tensions have bolstered defense capex.

Organic growth accounted for 16 of the 18-point total increase, with the remainder from our recent tuck-in acquisition of RoboForge Dynamics.

Geographically, North America, 42% of orders at $540 million, up 25% YoY. U.S. industrial capex is firing on all cylinders, with reshoring under the IRA and CHIPS Act driving $200 million in semiconductor and battery gigafactory orders. EMEA, 28% at $358 million, up 14% YoY, rebounded with wind OEMs awarding $100 million in nacelle assembly lines. Asia-Pacific, 25% at $320 million, up 15% YoY, led by China’s EV battery surge and India’s PLI scheme. Rest of World, 5% at $64 million, flat YoY.

Our ending order backlog now stands at $3.4 billion, up 24% YoY and providing 10 months of revenue visibility. Secular trends in Industry 4.0 and sustainability, supply chain resilience with 80% nearshoring, and pricing power with ASPs up 5% YoY are fueling this. We expect Q4 order intake of $1.35-$1.45 billion, implying FY24 full-year growth of 20%+.

Good morning, everyone. As your CFO, I'll now turn to our supply chain constraints and component availability updates—a topic that's been top-of-mind for investors given the sector's exposure to global disruptions. I'm pleased to report meaningful progress here, which has directly supported our record Q3 bookings of $2.8 billion, up 15% year-over-year, and allowed us to ship 92% of committed orders on time, versus just 78% in Q2 2023 amid peak shortages.

The industry has faced persistent headwinds from semiconductor scarcity, volatile commodity pricing, and logistics bottlenecks—exacerbated by U.S.-China trade tensions, Red Sea disruptions, and Europe's energy crunch. Our BOM for core products like PrecisionCNC Series 5000 lathes and ServoDrive hydraulic systems relies heavily on high-end microcontrollers, power semiconductors, and structural steel alloys. In Q1 2023, average lead times for automotive-grade MOSFETs and IGBTs stretched to 22 weeks, idling 15% of assembly lines.

Today, Q3 lead times for critical electronics have compressed to 7-9 weeks—a 65% improvement—thanks to a multi-pronged strategy. Inventory turns stabilized at 4.2x, with strategic stockpiles covering 14 weeks of demand.

Semiconductors and electronics, 45% of COGS exposure, saw allocation constraints ease, with wafer fab utilization dropping to 85%. We've secured 120% of Q4 needs through long-term agreements with TSMC and Samsung, locking pricing flat YoY. We're qualifying U.S.-based Intel for 20% of microcontroller volume by H1 2025.

Metals and alloys, 30% of COGS, moderated with HRC prices falling 12% QoQ to $650/ton. We've shifted 25% of steel sourcing to U.S. mills, cutting lead times to 5 weeks. In APAC, hedging 70% of 2025 needs.

Logistics and sub-assemblies, 15% of COGS, saw container rates plummet 35% QoQ, but we've optimized via SAP S/4HANA and AI analytics for 15% better OTD.

Regionally, North America supply chains are most resilient, with Mexico nearshoring; EMEA challenging with German delays, pivoted to Turkish alternates; APAC costs down 7% YoY.

We've invested $250M YTD in resilience: supplier diversification portal, in-house ASICs, digital twin optimization, and resilience hubs.

These efforts expanded margins 220bps to 28.1%, with Q4 revenue guiding to $2.9B-$3.1B and backlog at $7.2B. Long-term, 40% nearshored by 2027 supports 10-12% growth.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before we open it up to Q&A, I'd like to provide some color on our operating margin guidance for Q4 and the full fiscal year 2024, which reflects the strength of our Industrial Automation and Heavy Machinery segments amid a resilient manufacturing backdrop.

In Q3, we delivered an adjusted operating margin of 12.5%, up 140 basis points year-over-year and ahead of our guidance midpoint. This was driven by a 210 bps gross margin expansion to 28.7%, fueled by favorable product mix—particularly our high-margin robotic palletizers and CNC machining centers, which grew 18% sequentially—and pricing actions averaging 4.2% across our backlog. SG&A came in at 16.2% of sales, benefiting from disciplined headcount management.

For Q4, we expect adjusted operating margins of 13.0% to 13.5%, implying 50 to 100 bps sequential expansion. This assumes revenue of $1.45 billion to $1.50 billion. Gross margin tailwinds to 29.0%-29.5%, supported by de-risking, with 70% of Q4 inputs fixed-price. OpEx leverage to 15.8%-16.1% of sales, with $18 million in lean sigma savings. North America anchors at ~15%, EMEA ~50 bps headwind, Asia-Pacific 11%.

For full year 2024, raising to 12.8%-13.2%, ~200 bps over FY23. Initiatives: Industry 4.0 ramp with $120M capex, sustainability pivot with 30% green bookings, M&A discipline.

Risks include China fab cuts or Red Sea issues, but strong liquidity positions us well.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow. Now, I will hand over to Lisa Chen, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Chen (COO):
Thank you, David. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service. Building on the supply chain progress David outlined, we've achieved 92% on-time delivery through diversification and digital tools, ramping utilization to 87% across facilities. We're leveraging data analytics from our Nexus OS and EdgeControl platforms to identify areas for improvement, like reducing scrap by 15% via digital twins, and drive operational excellence. We are also investing in employee training and development to build a highly skilled workforce, particularly in AI integration for predictive maintenance, ensuring we capture the full value from our record backlog.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Raj Patel, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Raj Patel (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. We're developing solutions to improve predictive maintenance and optimize our customer's operations, like the IntelliSense suite reducing downtime by 30% and DynamicsEdge for as-a-service models now in 40% of bookings. Our new RoboForge robotic welding cells and Lynx EV platform are exceeding expectations, with impact including 25% cycle time reductions and 20% TCO savings, powering wins in EV and data center builds.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Raj Patel (CTO):
Thanks, John. Automation spending remains robust, particularly in discrete automation where orders surged 28% YoY. We're seeing accelerated investments from automotive OEMs ramping EV lines and hyperscalers building AI data centers, favoring our FANUC-compatible cobots and AI-driven RoboForge cells that cut cycle times 25%. Electrification is now 25% of orders, up sharply, with predictive platforms like NexGen delivering 15-20% OEE gains. We expect this to continue with capex recovery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

David Thompson (CFO):
Thanks, Emily. Our strategy mirrors what I detailed earlier: proactive pricing averaging 6.5-7.2% YoY, outpacing 18% input inflation through value-based selling tied to ApexEdge software. Hedging 50% of 2024 commodities, dual-sourcing steel from U.S. mills, and value engineering shaved BOM costs 3%. Aftermarket at 22% of revenue with 45% margins hedges volatility. This delivered 230 bps gross expansion, guiding to more in H2.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee (Barclays):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Absolutely, Mike. Sustainability is core, with eco-friendly waterless coolants winning $250M ESG contracts and 40% of revenue from low-carbon products. Electrification in 25% of orders, hydrogen-ready compressors, and green capex like Lynx EV platforms align with IRA and EU Green Deal. Our nearshoring cuts freight emissions, and REPowerEU wins position us for more. We're on track for structural improvements.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Dynamics Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

Impact of price-cost dynamics on margins (e.g., raw material costs, pricing actions).
Total order intake and year-over-year growth rate.

aspect_summary.Book-to-bill ratio and trends: Q3 company-wide book-to-bill ratio of 1.18x-1.28x, improved sequentially from 1.12x-1.18x in Q2 and YoY from 1.05x in Q3 2023; strongest since Q4 2021. Trailing 12-month at 1.14x. Segment trends: Factory Automation 1.25x, Precision Machining 1.15x, Material Handling 1.10x. Regional: NA 1.22x, EMEA 1.16x, APAC 1.08x. Expect 1.15x-1.20x through year-end.
aspect_summary.Order intake and book-to-bill trends by: Construction (42% of orders): $1.20B, +22% YoY, book-to-bill 1.45x. Mining (28%): $800M, +9% YoY, book-to-bill 1.35x. Agriculture (18%): $510M, flat YoY/+8% seq, book-to-bill 1.10x. Other (12%): +14% oil & gas, +10% power gen, book-to-bill 1.20x avg.
aspect_summary.Revenue performance by geographic region: Q3 revenue $1.35B, +15% YoY. NA (47%): $602M, +18% YoY/+7% QoQ. Europe (24%): $307M, +8% YoY/flat QoQ. APAC (25%): $320M, +16% YoY/+6% QoQ. RoW (4%): $51M, +12% YoY/+3% QoQ.
aspect_summary.Impact of price-cost dynamics on margins: Raw material costs +12-18% YoY (steel +22%, aluminum +15%, copper +25%, semis +10%). Pricing actions +6.5-7.2% (higher 8-10% on premium), outpacing inputs by 450bps. Resulted in gross margin expansion 210-230bps to 28.2-28.5%, via hedging (50%), diversification, value engineering, aftermarket hedge.
aspect_summary.Total order intake and year-over-year gr: Q3 total order intake $1.28B-$2.85B, +12-18% YoY (9th straight double-digit quarter). Trailing 12m record highs. Q4 guide $1.35-3.1B; FY24 +20%+.
aspect_summary.Supply chain constraints and component a: Constraints eased significantly: semi lead times -65% to 7-9 weeks, on-time delivery 92% (vs 78% prior year). Secured 120% Q4 semi needs, steel lead times 5 weeks, container rates -35% QoQ. Progress via diversification (25% US steel), hedging (70% APAC), stockpiles (14 weeks), $250M investments; utilization 87%.
aspect_summary.Operating margin guidance for the next q: Q4 (next quarter): 13.0-13.5% adjusted (50-100bps seq expansion). FY2024 full year: raised to 12.8-13.2% (~200bps over FY23). Q3 actual 12.5%, +140bps YoY.
